overall: Atlanta started the day under persistent overcast (OVC from midnight through ~06:52 ET), which suppressed overnight cooling and kept temperatures unusually elevated in the 71-74°F range. By 07:52 ET, cloud cover had broken significantly to FEW (38%), and temperatures have stalled near 73.9°F — the running max — with essentially zero warming velocity as of 08:00 ET. The active severe weather alerts (flash flood warnings, flood watch) are focused well south/southeast of Atlanta metro in central and coastal Georgia, so no immediate tropical or severe weather disruption to Atlanta is expected.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP model consensus is tight and slightly below the NWS text forecast: ECMWF at 84.4°F, HRRR at 85.1°F, and NBM at 83.9°F, all clustering in the 84-85°F range versus the NWS-stated high of 86°F. Observed temperatures overnight ran warmer than the NWS-forecast low of 68°F (actual observed minimum ~71-72°F), suggesting a moist, cloudy overnight that may have loaded the low-level atmosphere with additional moisture and could modestly limit peak afternoon heating.
max_temp_prediction: With clouds clearing through the morning and good solar insolation expected through the early-to-mid afternoon, temperatures should rise steadily from the current ~74°F toward the mid-80s. The primary cap on the high is the high dewpoints (~71-72°F) limiting sensible heat gain and the 20% PoP for afternoon convection (2-4 PM window) that could arrest warming before the typical NWP-modeled peak around 16-17h ET. Weighing NWP model consensus (84-85°F) against the NWS text forecast of 86°F and the probability distribution peaking in the 86-87°F bucket, the best estimate is near 85°F with moderate confidence — a miss toward 83°F is possible if afternoon convection arrives early, while 87°F is possible if skies remain clear and the afternoon storm threat stays suppressed.
